newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends weaker, Dec hits new contract low.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends weaker, Dec hits new contract low.

text.p: NYCE cotton ended sharply down amid heavy speculative selling that pressured most contracts to fresh lifetime lows, trading sources said.
Benchmark December broke through nearby support at 75.00 cents and triggered stops that carried the contract through all support targets and to the day's low of 73.75 cents.
The previous contract low was 73.85 cents.

Scale-down mill buying stalled losses but remained too thin to support the market. Dealers said follow-through selling could pressure prices further on Tuesday, and pegged support in December at 70.00 cents.
The most-active month ended down 2.05 cents at 73.75 cents per lb, having ranged from 76.05 to 73.70 cents. The rest of the board settled 2.03 to 0.95 weaker.
An estimated 28,000 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Thursday's official 14,974 lots.

Analysts said the failure of the December contract to pierce its recent high of 77.65 cents, coupled with a dearth of supportive fundamental news such as weather or pest problems, set the market up for a sharp selloff.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture will issue its weekly progress report at 1600 EDT amid expectations for an improving U.S. cotton crop.
Benefical rains were noted over the weekend in West Texas, Georgia and Alabama.
